h1: The 6 Best Shark Cordless Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Shark Cordless Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six Shark cordless vacuums compared on listed runtime, auto-empty docks and price tier, with a clear pick for every budget.
summary: The Shark PowerDetect Reveal Clean & Empty stick is the best Shark cordless vacuum, listing 70 minutes and an auto-empty dock in the $100 to $200 bucket. The standard PowerDetect matches the runtime for a tier more. The PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus is the dockless mid-range choice at 50 minutes, and the Shark Pet is the entry point.
intro: Shark's cordless range is where model names stop helping. A PowerDetect, a PowerDetect Reveal and a plain Clean & Empty stick can look like siblings, yet they land in different price buckets with different runtimes and docks. Two sticks with the same battery minutes can sit a full tier apart, and an auto-empty base can raise the price without adding a single minute to the clock.

We ranked six genuine Shark cordless models on listed runtime, whether the name includes a Clean & Empty system, and price tier. Duplicate listings of the same model were counted once. Runtime figures are best-case claims from the listings, so read each one as a ceiling, not a promise, and weigh the dock and bucket alongside the minutes before you buy.

products.name: Shark PowerDetect Reveal Clean & Empty Cordless Stick Vacuum &
products.verdict: Seventy listed minutes and an auto-empty system in the cheaper bucket.
products.description:
The PowerDetect Reveal Clean & Empty is the model to start from. It lists 70 minutes of runtime as a cordless stick and bundles a Clean & Empty system that moves debris from the bin into a base, so you handle dust far less often. That dock is what makes a stick vacuum feel like a lower-chore appliance in a busy house.

It leads because it matches the longest runtime in this group while costing a tier less than the plain PowerDetect. The $100 to $200 bucket also undercuts the $200 to $500 Clean & Empty stick at 40 minutes by a wide margin on value, since you get 30 more minutes for less.

Choose it for a larger home that wants minutes and a self-emptying base. The caveat is that 70 minutes is a best-case figure, and high-power modes cut it. A lower bucket may also mean fewer inclusions, so read what ships in the box.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want long runtime and a self-emptying dock on a tighter budget.
products.skipIf: You prefer the more established PowerDetect listing.

products.name: Shark PowerDetect Clean & Empty Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The same 70 minutes as the leader, in the $200-500 bucket.
products.description:
The standard PowerDetect Clean & Empty lists the same 70 minutes and the same auto-empty system as the Reveal above, in the $200 to $500 bucket. It is the better-established listing, which matters if you want a model with a longer track record in owner reports.

It lands second because the numbers are identical and the price is higher. Against the plain Clean & Empty stick at 40 minutes, it is far stronger, but against its own Reveal sibling it gives you nothing extra on paper. That makes it a preference pick, not a performance pick.

Buy it if you specifically want the PowerDetect configuration and the Reveal naming puts you off. Otherwise, take the cheaper model and spend the difference on spare filters. The dust cup and dock details are not spelled out in the listing, so double check that the base is included before ordering.
products.idealFor: Owners who want the PowerDetect configuration specifically.
products.skipIf: You want the same minutes for less.

products.name: Shark PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus Cordless Vacuum
products.verdict: Fifty listed minutes at the $100-200 price point.
products.description:
The PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus is the straightforward Shark. It lists 50 minutes of runtime and a cordless build in the $100 to $200 bucket, with no dock to find space for in a closet. For many apartments, skipping the base is a feature, not a flaw.

It ranks third because it trails the top two by 20 minutes and has no Clean & Empty system in its name, so you empty the bin yourself. Against the IZ363HT below, it lists the same 50 minutes for a lower bucket, which is why it sits ahead. It is the value anchor in the middle of the lineup.

Buy it for a mid-size home where 50 minutes covers a full clean and a dock would just take up room. Check what attachments the box includes before assuming a crevice tool or pet brush is supplied. Skip it if emptying the bin is the chore you hate most.
pros: No dock to find space for
products.idealFor: Mid-size homes on a mid-range budget.

products.name: Shark Cordless Vacuum Cleaner - Blue - IZ363HT
products.verdict: Fifty minutes, but in the pricier $200-500 bucket.
products.description:
The IZ363HT is the established model number in this ranking. It lists a 50 minute runtime and cordless build in the $200 to $500 bucket, and a long-running model code means plenty of owner history to read before you commit.

It ranks fourth because it matches the PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus on minutes while costing a tier more. Older designs often carry the premium of a brand-name listing rather than new hardware, and nothing in the specs says this one cleans better. Its only edge over the 40 minute sticks below is ten extra minutes.

Choose it only if you specifically want this model, perhaps because a replacement battery or part is easier to find under a familiar code. Otherwise the cheaper 50 minute Shark gets you the same runtime. The caveat is simple: you pay more for a design that is not newer, and no dock is listed.
products.idealFor: Buyers who already know and like this model.
products.skipIf: You would rather save a price tier.

products.name: Shark Clean & Empty Cordless Stick Vacuum & Auto-Empty System
products.description:
This Clean & Empty stick sells convenience at the cost of runtime. It lists an auto-empty system and a cordless stick body, but only 40 minutes of battery, in the $200 to $500 bucket. For a small home, 40 minutes is often plenty, and the base removes the bin-emptying chore.

It places fifth because the PowerDetect models deliver 70 minutes with the same dock idea, and one of them costs less. This one buys the base without the minutes, so the value case is weak unless your floor area is small. It does beat the Pet stick below on the dock alone.

Buy it for a small apartment or townhouse where bin emptying is what bothers you. Skip it if you clean more than a couple of rooms per session. The runtime is the ceiling here, and boost modes will shorten the 40 minutes further.
products.idealFor: Small homes that value a self-emptying bin.

products.name: Shark Pet Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The simplest Shark here: 40 minutes, no dock, $100-200.
products.description:
The Shark Pet Cordless Stick is the baseline. It lists 40 minutes of runtime on a cordless stick, with no dock named, in the $100 to $200 bucket. It is light on setup and sits in the lowest-cost tier among the Sharks here, so you can put it in a closet and forget the base.

It finishes last because every model above adds minutes, a dock or both. Its pet name suggests a focus on hair, but the listing gives no specific brush detail, so we treat it as a generic stick on the numbers. At 40 minutes it ties the Clean & Empty stick above while skipping the dock, which is the trade.

Choose it for an apartment or as a second vacuum for stairs and cars. Do not expect it to cover a large home on one charge, and plan to empty the bin by hand after every use.

whatMatters.detail: Runtime is how many minutes a full battery lasts. It matters because a short runtime forces a mid-clean recharge, which breaks your routine. Shark lists 40 to 70 minutes across this group. Read the minutes in the title or bullets and treat them as best-case, since boost and carpet modes shorten them noticeably. Ask whether the battery is removable if you want a spare.

A Clean & Empty system moves debris from the vacuum into a base, so you stop opening a dirty bin over the trash. It is a real convenience for allergy sufferers and busy homes. Look for Clean & Empty or Auto-Empty in the model name, then check that the base is included and not sold separately. Also confirm the bag or bin type, since it sets how often you pay for refills.

Shark sells near-identical names in different price tiers, so you can pay a tier more for the same minutes. The PowerDetect and PowerDetect Reveal both list 70 minutes, yet one costs $100 to $200 and the other $200 to $500. Compare the full model name and runtime, never just the brand line, and look at the bucket before you trust a cheaper-sounding name.

Floor area and number of rooms decide how many minutes you need. A small apartment rarely needs 70 minutes, while a larger house with stairs does. Match the listed runtime to the cleaning session you actually do, add margin for boost modes, and do not pay for minutes you will not use. Count the rooms and stairs once, then divide by the minutes listed.

Price buckets here run from $100 to $200 up to $200 to $500, and the right bucket depends on whether the dock and runtime matter to you. A higher bucket does not guarantee a better machine, as the IZ363HT shows. Check the bucket on the listing, then compare minutes and dock before deciding. Read the box contents list to see whether attachments are included.

faq.q: Why do two Shark Pet listings exist?
faq.a: The same model can appear in different bundles and price tiers across listings. We counted each model once, which is why the Shark Pet appears as a single entry rather than several. Check bundle contents before you buy.

faq.q: Is 70 minutes worth the extra cost?
faq.a: Only for bigger homes. The PowerDetect Reveal's 70 minutes helps in a multi-room house, while the Shark Pet or the 40 minute Clean & Empty stick covers a small apartment without trouble, and the savings are real.

faq.q: Do I need an auto-empty dock?
faq.a: It is a convenience, not a requirement. Clean & Empty on the PowerDetect Reveal saves emptying the bin by hand, but the PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus skips the base and costs the same $100 to $200 bucket, so you can choose by chore.

It lists no runtime figure, so it cannot be compared on paper with the others here. Every model we ranked states minutes, which is the number our comparison depends on, so a missing figure rules a model out.

faq.q: How accurate is the runtime figure?
faq.a: Treat it as a best case. Higher power modes shorten it, so a 70 minute PowerDetect may run noticeably less on carpet, and the 40 minute models can feel short in a bigger home. Boost mode shortens it further.

faq.q: Are the Reveal models different from the plain ones?
faq.a: They carry a different name in the lineup, and the Reveal sibling costs less in the listings we reviewed. Check what is included in each box, since a lower bucket may omit attachments or a charging cradle.

finalTake: For most homes, the Shark PowerDetect Reveal Clean & Empty is the right Shark cordless vacuum, with 70 listed minutes and an auto-empty dock in the $100 to $200 bucket. Pay for the standard PowerDetect only if you prefer its listing. Take the PowerPro Flex Reveal Plus if you want 50 minutes and no base, and the Shark Pet as a simple second vacuum.
